page: Amazon Web Services m6in.16xlarge is a general-purpose, network-optimized server powered by the Nitro hypervisor. It features 64 vCPUs and 32 physical cores based on the x86_64 Intel Xeon 8375C processor running at 3.5 GHz. The system includes 256.0 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per core. This instance does not include local storage or dedicated GPUs, relying instead on network-attached storage.

Benchmark data indicates strong multi-core performance, with stress-ng multi-core CPU and PassMark CPU scores placing in the top 25%. The Intel Xeon processor supports advanced vector instructions, including AVX-512 and cryptography acceleration via AES and SHA_NI, which contribute to strong performance in PassMark extended instructions and encryption tests. Memory bandwidth benchmarks for large block reads and writes fall within the average range, while static web serving throughput and software compilation with Clang demonstrate strong performance.

The primary tradeoff of the m6in.16xlarge is the complete absence of local NVMe storage, requiring workloads to utilize network-attached EBS volumes. However, this is mitigated by a high baseline network bandwidth of 100 Gbps. From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the server offers a dense allocation of compute and memory resources suitable for enterprise-scale workloads without the overhead of dedicated GPU hardware. It is well-suited for database operations, multi-threaded software compilation, high-throughput static web serving, and medium-scale LLM text generation.
